about: Every pushed update gets the next version (newest first). The game shows the newest one in the bottom-right corner; the admin page lists them all.

versions.title: Sign in for the boards, and a cleaner admin page
notes: After a run played as a guest, the results screen says the run is not on the leaderboards and offers a Discord sign-in so the next ones are (it counts on the admin Overview's Guests card as a sign-in asked for the leaderboard).

The admin page looks new: the Inter typeface with monospaced numbers, rounded cards, a pinned header that blurs what scrolls under it, underlined tabs, tinted status pills and calmer buttons. On a phone only the tabs stay pinned, and the Visibility rows stack so every switch is in reach.

versions.title: Play without signing in
notes: New players can try the game straight away: on a server, the zones open to guests play without a Discord sign-in. The District is open to guests from the start; every other zone, co-op and the Mazoku card hunt still ask for Discord.

The admin page's Visibility tab has a second switch on every map: Guests can play, or Discord login. It only counts while the map is live. Co-op always needs a Discord sign-in, with no switch to open it.

A guest sees the free zones first, marked FREE, and the rest marked SIGN IN. Picking one of those, WITH FRIENDS or the card hunt asks for the sign-in, with the free zone offered beside it. After signing in you come back to the zone, the mode or the co-op invite you had picked.
First time here: a short tour of the title screen (the zones, how to play, what a sign-in opens). Skip it at any time, or see it again from CONTROLS. On a phone each step is one line along the edge.

Guest runs are recorded like anyone's (time played, maps, outcomes, device and frame rate) but never rank on the leaderboards. The admin Overview has a new Guests card: guest visitors and players, the tour and sign-in prompts, and how many guests went on to sign in.

versions.title: The admin page controls what players see
notes: A new Visibility tab on the admin page (it takes over Maps and Cinematics): every map, every cinematic, co-op itself, each way to host it, Free roam, the Mazoku card hunt, each Sakura District story mission, Aurelia herself, the bestiary and its Style Lab - each live for everyone or admin only. Everything new starts the way it was, so nothing changed for players until an admin switches it.

What is switched off is gone for players everywhere: off the title screen and the co-op lobby, out of the bestiary and the leaderboards, and refused by the server (a run, a co-op session, a page). Switching something off ends the co-op sessions it closes that no admin owns. An admin still sees and plays everything, marked ADMIN ONLY.
A player is only ever told what is open; the names of what is hidden are not sent to them, and the game no longer carries the update notes inside it.
Fixed: a link with a session code no longer keeps a player on a map that is admin only, and the boards of an admin-only map are no longer readable by players.
Only an admin who owns a session can invite players past what is switched off; a player who takes over the session cannot.

versions.title: Aurelia walks the valley (admin only)
notes: Aurelia herself is on her map: red hair burning to orange, a white dress and gold wings of flame folded at her back. She walks a few steps ahead of the squad, and the infected hunt her like anyone else.

She cannot die. Killed, she falls and a red spider lily opens where she lay; she lies in the ash for 8 seconds, longer for every death in a row (12, 18, 27, never more than 30), and infected standing on her ashes hold her down. Then she rises in a column of fire, and the burst throws back and burns everything within 6 metres.
Solo and co-op: in co-op the server runs her and everyone sees the same Aurelia.
Until she has a model of her own she wears a stand-in from the cast, dressed in her colours.
Anyone killed up on a raised floor now falls there instead of dropping through to the ground below.

versions.title: AURELIA, a new map (admin only), and phones keep the middle clear
notes: AURELIA, the first map of a new story: a round river valley under an equinox moon, where three stone terraces climb in rings to the Phoenix Shrine on the summit. Ten flights of stairs, torii, stone lanterns, rest pavilions, red lantern posts and black spider lilies everywhere, and across the river a far shore glowing with lilies that nobody can reach.

Its mission: power the river relay on the east bank, climb the Lantern Terrace and the Shrine Steps to put down the Shrine Keeper at the summit, then hold the west bank until the bird lands, while the black bloom spreads from the back of the valley late in the night. Athy and piryriry cross with you; Marv03K, .maidlover. and Anya are caged on the riverbank. Solo and co-op, and on the leaderboards.
AURELIA is admin only until it is opened from the admin page's Maps switches. The story it was built for (Aurelia herself, the lily rites, Undying Grace) comes later.

On phones, banners and radio lines no longer cover the middle of the screen on any map: they share one short line along the top edge, one piece at a time, split at word breaks so nothing is lost. Desktop is unchanged.
Every update is now checked for a server that will not start before it goes out (the kind of mistake that kept 0.4.311 offline).

versions.title: The server starts again
notes: 0.4.311 never went live: three of the server's lines were committed in the wrong places, so it could not start and the game was down until this update. They are back where they belong, and the admin page's Cinematics switches are registered as their own routes again.
Everything 0.4.311 brought (Slime Hollow, admin only for now, and a public or admin-only switch for every cinematic) goes live with this update.

versions.title: Slime Hollow, and a switch for every cinematic
notes: SLIME HOLLOW (hollow.html), a 76-second anime tragedy, ready for the CINEMATICS page and admin only for now. A burned village, the Iron Choir at its gate, and the night the Hollow Slime takes Kael - the black ooze climbs him, turns his hair long and white and becomes his cloak, his spikes and a wall of cyan crystal fire - until his sworn brother Raigen catches his blade and brings him back. There is no happy ending.

A cast of seven original characters (Kael, Raigen, Suzu, Goro, Nagi, Oriha, Captain Auren) and crowds of over three hundred: the army marches, halts, mutters, loses its torches row by row, is thrown by the spikes, breaks and runs or kneels; the village's wounded, fighters, children and elders react through it all. The crowds thin out on LOW graphics.

Its own colour: the world drains to ink and manga screentone when Kael gives the order, with only the Hollow's cyan left alive (and Raigen's crimson lightning at the catch), impact frames on the clink and the whack, speed lines, and a cold grey dawn that gives no colour back.

A very dark orchestral score cut to the film (Lyria 3), voiced lines for the cast and the army (ElevenLabs v4), synthesised effects; the same controls as Excalibur (film camera, walk, fly, slow motion, loop, volumes, graphics, full screen), its own loading and start screens and link preview. The cast is in the Bestiary's CINEMATICS section.

Every cinematic can be made public or admin only from the admin page's new Cinematics tab (Excalibur stays public, Slime Hollow starts admin only). A private film is hidden from players on the CINEMATICS page, in the bestiary and in the sitemap, and its page, sounds and images are refused to anyone but an admin; admins see it marked ADMIN ONLY.

versions.title: Excalibur opens like a film
notes: Excalibur loads everything first on its own loading screen (the game's layout in its violet and red), then opens on a start screen with the camera circling the knight; it plays only when you press PLAY, and the sound and graphics settings work there too.
No more stutter as the fight begins: every effect is prepared before the film starts. A Graphics setting (AUTO, LOW, MED, HIGH) sits under the volumes; AUTO suits the device and adjusts as it runs.
On a computer drawing without its graphics card (hardware acceleration off), the loading screen says so and how to turn it on.

Shared links to Excalibur show their own title, description and a picture from the film; the film ends with its credit, directed by MiMs & QuorX; the phone layout is more compact; and the page no longer flashes unstyled while it loads.

versions.title: Visits per page, and Excalibur's starting volumes
notes: Visits now record which page they are to: the game, Excalibur or the Bestiary (both now count their visits); the admin page shows visits, unique visitors and the share on phones for each page. Earlier visits count as the game's.
Excalibur starts at gentler volumes: master 80%, music and effects 70%, voices 85% (levels you have set yourself are kept).

versions.title: The cast of Excalibur in the Bestiary
notes: The Bestiary has a CINEMATICS section: the Black Knight (guard, strike, dash, leap, and her Excalibur charge with the blade of light) and the Giant (roar, walk, cleave, slam, block, kneel).
BESTIARY in the menu now opens a codex page first: every section of the field guide on a card, each opening the 3D bestiary on its first entry, or the whole guide.
Excalibur and the Bestiary keep themselves current: when they open, or you come back to them, they check which version is live and reload once if they are behind (a phone's saved copy included).

versions.title: Cinematics, and updates that show at once
notes: A new CINEMATICS page in the menu, home to short films set apart from the game (more to come); Excalibur now lives there instead of in the menu itself.

Updates show at once: the pages are checked with the server on every visit, so a new version is never held back by the browser's copy, and Excalibur's score and voices download again whenever they change.

versions.title: Excalibur full screen
notes: The Excalibur scene has a full screen button (top of the buttons on the right) and a G key; Esc or the button again leaves it. On Android phones it also turns the scene to landscape where the phone allows it (iPhones don't allow full screen for web pages, so the button hides there).

versions.title: Excalibur sound fixes
notes: The Excalibur score no longer drops out before the blast: the quiet heartbeat stretch as she calls the blade is fuller (about 5 dB), with a cleaner hand-off into the final act.
The music never jumps back after a slow frame: the scene catches up to the score instead, so heavy moments (the slams, the berserk roar, the beam) no longer make it stutter or repeat.

The giant's roars now land with a low boom and rumble; his roars no longer cut over her lines ("Is that all you have?", "Darkness... answer me."), and her whispered lines are lifted so they carry over the score.

versions.title: Excalibur v2
notes: The Excalibur scene is now a full 88-second battle in five acts. The fight: a circling exchange, his ground slam and her strike out of the sky, a shockwave she leaps, a blitz from every side with trails of light, him swatting her across the courtyard ("...Not yet."), blades locked in a fountain of sparks until she breaks it, and him going berserk in a red aura.

The charge now takes twenty seconds: darkness pours in from the whole courtyard, the rubble lifts into the air, he charges and her pressure throws him back, the blade goes overhead under a column of light and lightning, a blade of light grows out of the steel, everything falls quiet but a heartbeat, and she draws out "Exxx..." before "CALIBUR!".

The beam holds on him for four seconds and keeps swelling; his slab glows white-hot and shatters; then the blast turns the world white as a nuke and it comes back slowly to ruins: the ground torn open along the beam's path into a deep crater with a molten floor (you can walk and drop down into it), scorch marks, pillars thrown flat, charred stone and trees, fires burning and smoke rising.

The shadow around her is now streams of dark particles instead of tendrils. Her violet aura and his red rage are particles too, with faint violet ripples spreading over the ground from her feet; when she moves fast a streak of violet light follows her. The rubble his slams throw up is small and settles away in seconds, never passing through her, so the fight stays clear to see; while she charges the lifted rocks hover in a wide ring around her.

It opens as a film now. Press C (or FILM) to step out and walk or fly; switching the film on and off always puts you back where you were. LOOP (or L) turned off stops the scene in the ruins and hands you the world to explore, with the last act of the score playing on and only the fire and wind around you. Looping, it fades to black at the end and back in.

A new, more intense score in three acts cut to the scene, twelve new voice lines (the best takes from several per line), and new sound effects: grinding blades, a heartbeat, a ten-second charge and a swelling beam. The scene now runs on the music's clock, so a slow frame can no longer make the music stutter or repeat.

versions.title: Excalibur: a free-roam film set
notes: New page, apart from the game: Excalibur (freeroam.html, and EXCALIBUR on the title screen). A black-armoured knight and a giant play out one anime battle scene on a 32-second loop: the shadow rises, the giant charges, four sword clashes, she gathers the dark into her blade under a column of light, brings it down as a wave of black-red light, a cut to black, then the blast and the rings of light rising from the crater.

Walk anywhere through it, jump onto the ruins or fly over the courtyard (F), or press C for the film camera, which cuts it shot by shot the way the movie would. T plays it in slow motion and R starts it again. On a phone: a thumb stick on the left, look by dragging on the right, and a few buttons down the right edge.

Its own score, generated for the scene and cut to it so the music drops away under the beam and comes back with the blast; both characters are voiced (the best of several takes from three voice models); every sound effect is synthesised in the browser.
Built to run fast: a few dozen draw calls, effects animated on the graphics card, bloom only on what glows, and the resolution steps down by itself if frames run long.

versions.title: Security updates
notes: Behind the scenes only: the game server and the build tools are updated to their latest patch releases, which fix several published security issues. Nothing about how the game plays changes.
The automated test runs that play the game in a browser are brought up to date with the current menus, maps and rewards, and they now run on Windows too.

versions.title: Deploys find pnpm again
notes: Behind the scenes only: when the server has no pnpm on its path (it goes missing after a Node update), the deploy now uses the pnpm that ships with Node instead of stopping. This is what kept 0.4.300 from going live.

versions.title: Link previews and search
notes: Sharing the game link (Discord, X, WhatsApp, Slack, iMessage...) now shows a proper preview card: the title screen as players see it, with the game's name and a short description. The bestiary link gets one too.
Search engines get a description, a canonical address, a sitemap and a robots file (the admin page and the API stay out of search results), plus the game's details as structured data.
The game has its own tab icon now.

versions.title: More time on the Sakura District
notes: The Sakura District is the biggest map, so it gets more time: 20 minutes before the district is sealed (was 12), with the surge and the escalation pushed back to match. The story missions get the same.
KAIKA, the whole story across the whole map, gets 45 minutes.
A long run's time survived is no longer cut off at 24 minutes in your results.

versions.title: Enter and leave the metro on purpose
notes: The stairwells down to the metro and the lab no longer take you through when you walk into them: stand at the doorway and hold E - ENTER METRO / ENTER LAB going down, LEAVE METRO / LEAVE LAB coming back up. No more dropping underground by mistake in the middle of a fight. (The infected still follow you through.)

versions.title: Follow the petals: the Sakura District shows you the way, and a real metro
notes: A trail of glowing petals on the ground now leads you to whatever is next - KAIKA's chapter, or the operation's next contract and then the landing zone - round walls, through doors and down the right stairs, with a pillar of light over the goal. The Thousand Lanterns stays a secret you find yourself.
Orders are short now ("Metro: put the 3 fuses back"), and the radio waits for a lull in the fighting before it talks, so nothing important is said while you are being chewed on.

The metro is rebuilt as a real Japanese subway: tiled walls with the Sakura Line's stripe, automatic ticket gates, ticket machines under a fare map, the station office and its lost and found, pillars with the station nameboard, half-height platform gates, benches, drink machines, a departure board, adverts, a ribbed tunnel with cables and signals, and a proper train with doors and wheels.

New pickups that change the map: put the metro's three fuses back and the whole station lights up - ceilings, strips, boards, machines and the train's windows. Every shrine charm you take now raises a ring of glowing paper lanterns where it was, so you can see from afar which places are at peace.
KAIKA starts with a new chapter, LIGHTS OUT (twelve in all).
Fixed: infected chasing you down a stairwell could get stuck at the bottom when they could not see you from the stairs.

versions.title: Admins can switch any map off
notes: Admin page, Maps: every map can now be Live (every player can pick it) or Admin only - not just the Sakura District. At least one map always stays live.
A player whose map was switched off lands on the first live map next time they load the game.

versions.title: Sakura District co-op fixes
notes: Co-op on the Sakura District: the squad, power-ups, mystery boxes and drops now stay in sync for everyone (the Thousand Lanterns' state was overwriting them on every update).
KAIKA: if the shrine relay was already restored before the lanterns were lit, the bell can still be rung - the ending (and the helicopter) can no longer get stuck.

versions.title: KAIKA: the Sakura District's whole story, its own cast, and its own sounds
notes: NEW STORY - KAIKA: THE BLOOMING (pick it under STORY on the Sakura District, solo or co-op, open from the start): a dead shrine keeper calls from the shrine relay, and her five charms send you through every corner of Sakuragi - the metro, the hilltop school, the arcade, the canal, the Court's freight yard, the lab under the theatre - then to the sacred tree, the Crimson Empress, the Thousand Lanterns and home. Eleven chapters with a marker for each; the helicopter only comes once the dead are seen home.

Every kind of infected on the Sakura District now has a body and look of its own: the miko in red and white with her bells, the Oni red-skinned with an iron club, the Jorogumo with eight legs, the Kuchisake in a red coat and mask with her shears, the idol in her stage dress, the bloomed full of blossom, the rooted grown through with roots, commuters with their briefcases - and the Crimson Empress under her red parasol. The Kurenai Court wear the theatre's crimson. Yuzu and your co-op teammates have their own models too.

The notes are gone. The story is told on the radio instead (the first time you walk into each part of the district), and a FIELD FILE card shows the first time you meet each kind of infected: what it looks like, what it does, and why it is there. The pause menu's FIELD FILE has how the outbreak began, the story so far and every infected you have met. Only the festival scroll on the theatre stage is left to read.

New sounds for the district: the Kuchisake's whisper and shears, the Jorogumo skittering and hissing, the miko's bells, the idol's song, the Oni's roar and club, a bloomed bursting, a rooted tearing out of the ground, the Court's whistle, the Empress's wail, commuters' phones; the shrine relay's static, a koto for each chapter, wind chimes, crows and the station's old departure melody.
Fixed: picking a story mission on the title screen and pressing PLAY straight away started the normal operation instead.

versions.title: The new infected fall when they die, and a brighter FPS counter
notes: With NEW 3D MODELS (BETA) on, killed infected now fall and lie on the ground instead of freezing upright where they died.
Their attacks and stagger reactions now play their animations too (they were stuck in the pose they had before).
The FPS counter (Settings: SHOW FPS COUNTER) is bigger and bright on a dark backing, in its own spot above the objectives: green at 50 fps and above, yellow from 30, red below.

versions.title: 0.2: smoother on every device, and a new way to bring in models
notes: Auto graphics: the game picks a quality for your device (new Lite for older phones, new High+ for strong PCs), checks how it runs in the first seconds, and steps the resolution and then the quality up or down as you play - never in the middle of a defense, a horde or the extraction. Picking a quality in Settings turns it off.
Fewer draw calls on every map: plain-coloured surfaces now share materials, so the GPU has far less to do each frame.

The Sakura District runs much better: distant infected are drawn as one simple crowd instead of full anime models (the busiest view went from about 2.2 million triangles to under 400,000), far Kurenai Court members drop their models, and the district's signs and graffiti now share a few textures.
Co-op: the other players and the infected update 10 times a second as intended (it was about 7), so movement looks smoother.

New in Settings: NEW 3D MODELS (BETA) swaps in an animated infected and street props from a free art pack (Quaternius, CC0) on the District, the Forge and the Asylum. It is a first look at the new model system - try it and tell us whether to keep going.
The Kurenai Court's riflemen shoot a little less often and less accurately.
Story missions on the Sakura District are recorded in your stats but kept off the leaderboards (they start with a contract already done).

versions.title: The Sakura District, rebuilt: seven springs after the fall
notes: The Sakura District is now its own 256 x 132 m map: the station and its evacuation point, the hilltop school, the covered shopping arcade, the canal and its park, the shrine on its hill, the Kurenai Theatre and the freight yard, all overgrown with cherry trees under a pink dusk sky with petals in the air.

Floors above and below: climb the school to its roof, the karaoke house, the apartments and the container decks, and take the stairwells down into the metro and the lab under the theatre. The infected follow you up and down.
Nobody is left to rescue here. Hana and Yuzu deploy with you; in co-op, players take their places (three people at most), and teammates wear VRoid models too.
35 notes lie around the district telling what each place was, how it fell and what is left; everything you read goes in the new JOURNAL tab in the pause menu and is kept between runs.

New infected: commuters who keep their routine (walk past quietly), bloomed who burst into stinging petal clouds, rooted who wait under the petals, a masked stalker who only moves when you are not looking, jorogumo on the tunnel ceilings, a miko who screams the dead to her, a singing idol who slows you, and the huge oni.

The Kurenai Court: living people with the checkpoint's rifles, on the container decks and round their fires before the theatre. They keep their distance and shoot. The Crimson Empress now calls her bloomed to her.

An Easter egg, the Thousand Lanterns: some notes carry a sakura stamp. Follow them, and the night changes - with a hidden station, two relics (the Hanafubuki petal cannon and Raijin's Drum) and an altar at the end of it.
Finishing the Easter egg opens three story missions on the map: The Crimson Curtain, Last Train and Hanami, in solo and in co-op.

versions.title: Fights on the Sakura District stay sharp
notes: Fighting on the Sakura District no longer drops the picture to a blurry, pixelated mess: the game's automatic resolution drop now stops at 75% instead of 60%.

The anime-model infected cost far more to draw than the stock ones, which is what slowed fights down; the ones far from you now move at a lower rate, so the game stays smooth and the resolution holds up.

versions.title: 02 Cyberpunk joins the Sakura District
notes: Hana, the squad's rifle girl, now wears the first of the cast's own VRoid models: 02 Cyberpunk, a pink-haired girl with red horns in black techwear.
Until their own models are added, Yuzu and the three trapped girls (Aoi, Mei and Koharu) wear her too.
The infected and the Crimson Empress keep the stand-in model for now.

versions.title: The Sakura District's infected have women's voices
notes: The infected on the Sakura District no longer growl like the regular horde: they moan, sometimes breaking into sobs; giggle when they notice you; hiss on the chase; the runners scream; the armored ones growl in a torn woman's voice.
They yelp and whimper when hit, and die with a gasp and a rattle. Their boss, the Crimson Empress, roars with a shriek.
Like every sound in the game, the voices are synthesised: no recordings.

versions.title: A stand-in anime model for the Sakura District
notes: Until the cast's own VRoid models are added, every Sakura District character wears one stand-in anime model (pixiv's sample, whose licence allows it) instead of the old blocky stand-in figures: Hana, Yuzu, the survivors, the boss, and the infected tinted grey with red eyes.
Each character switches to their own model as soon as its file is added to public/anime/ (see the README there).

versions.title: Admin stats without the admins
notes: A Hide admins switch at the top of the admin page leaves the admins' own visits, runs, cards and co-op sessions out of the Overview, the Runs list and the Players list, to see how the game looks without them playing.
The switch is remembered on that browser.

versions.title: Sakura District, admin-only for now
notes: A new zone, the Sakura District: the District's streets at blossom dusk with an anime cast - Hana and Yuzu of the Hanabi unit deploy with you, Aoi, Mei and Koharu wait to be freed, and the boss is the Crimson Empress.
Its people and infected wear VRoid models (.vrm files in public/anime/); the infected are tinted grey with glowing eyes. Until the models are added, the stock figures stand in.
Fewer infected at once on this zone (24, 12 on phones), because each anime model costs much more to draw.
Admin-only for now: players do not see it. Admins can play it (marked ADMIN ONLY) and open it to everyone from the admin page's new Maps tab.
The bestiary has the Sakura cast, a male model slot for later, and a Style Lab of six other art styles to compare.

versions.title: Leaderboards that show their history
notes: The leaderboards open at Normal, where every run from before difficulties were recorded is counted, and each difficulty button shows how many players it ranks.
An empty board says which difficulties do have runs.
Admins see a line saying their own runs are not on the boards.

versions.title: Simpler leaderboards
notes: Every leaderboard is read at one difficulty, so an Easy run and a Nightmare run are never ranked together; the page opens at the zone and difficulty you play.
Fewer choices: zone, difficulty, solo or co-op (solo now counts Standard Mazoku runs too), fastest escape or most kills, and a 'this version only' box. Most headshots and the version list are gone.

Each row is one line - rank, player, result. Point at it (tap on a phone) and a card shows the run: escaped or fell and the time, kills, headshots, contracts, mode, difficulty, device, version and date.
Runs from before the difficulty was recorded count as Normal. The admin page lists the 12 boards (switching one off hides it at every difficulty).

versions.title: tomoe's rounded hair
notes: tomoe's spiky hair is now soft and rounded: a full white dome with a rounded fringe over the brow.

versions.title: Join a co-op run mid-game, and a phone title that fits
notes: A co-op session's code keeps working once the run is under way: people can come in as players (while a seat is free) or as spectators, as the owner allows - play or watch, watch only, or nobody. Anyone the owner invites always can. The owner changes it in the lobby or, mid-game, in the pause menu, which also shows the code and copies the invite link.
Only server-hosted sessions take people mid-game: a self-hosted session runs on its owner's device, so it is joined from its lobby only.
The co-op scoreboard (Tab) shows the session's code and who may join.

On a phone the title screen fits the screen without scrolling: the menu is icons only (down the left edge held sideways, a tab bar along the bottom held upright), and the page shows the zone, the big button and the zones as small buttons.
Explore is called Free roam again on the title screen.

versions.title: A simpler title screen, and leaderboards
notes: A new title screen, laid out like a game launcher over the live map: a side menu (Play, With friends, Explore, Leaderboards, Bestiary, Controls, Settings, your account), the zone as the headline with one big button, and the zones and what you do on them below. Squad skill and the Mazoku card hunt sit behind More options. On a phone the side menu becomes a strip along the top.
Visitors who are not signed in see one clear button - Sign in with Discord to play - and can still look around the zones, the leaderboards and the bestiary first.

Leaderboards for every zone, for solo, Mazoku and co-op runs: fastest extraction, most kills and most headshots, each player's best run once, filtered by game version and difficulty. Admins never appear on them, and banned players drop off.
Admin page: the co-op sessions live right now open the Overview tab (refreshed every 15 seconds), and a new Leaderboards tab switches every board, or any of them, off and on.
The weapon in hand no longer shows behind the title screen.

versions.title: The Hearth round the helipad
notes: The Hearth is now the landing zone: a walled yard round the helipad with a gate standing open in the middle of every wall. The run starts there, the helicopter lands there, and the last stand comes at it from all four sides.
One sentry gun on a tower in the yard's corner covers the whole yard and every gate (it never fires on a boss).

The people you save take up a weak shotgun each at the Hearth and shoot the infected that get near them; their kills pay nothing, like the sentry's. The member who turns into the reborn does it right there among them.
Anya has a new look: a messy dark-blue bob, amber eyes, a white school blouse with a black ribbon, a pleated skirt, and a bass guitar in her hands - her gun at the Hearth is her bass.

Dark interiors are lit properly: indoors, the lamps in the room you are in now come before the brighter street lamps outside (which only shone through the walls), and the seven foundries have hanging work lamps.
Fixed rescued people sometimes staying drawn at their room's back door instead of appearing at the Hearth.

versions.title: New looks for tomoe, Anya and .maidlover.
notes: tomoe gets an anime look: a shock of spiky white hair, blue eyes, a loose white tunic over a navy turtleneck, blue shorts, purple sneakers and a yellow skateboard slung across the back.
Anya gets an anime look: a blue bob with a white streak, amber eyes behind round glasses, white headphones, a white star clip and a dark hoodie.

.maidlover. joins the Forge: they can now be one of the two who deploy with you (or be holed up with the others), with an anime look of long pink hair, small red horns, a white headband and a red uniform with an orange tie.

versions.title: No rank titles
notes: Nobody's rank is shown any more: the name tags over Vulcan's people (and the ending's lists) just say VULCAN, the squad objective is KEEP THE SQUAD ALIVE, and the menu, the bestiary and the ledger no longer name anyone's role.
The honours wall inside Vulcan HQ is gone.

versions.title: A more compact admin page
notes: The admin page is split into tabs (Overview, Runs, Players, Co-op, Reports, Versions); the open tab is kept in the address, so a link or a reload lands on it.
Denser layout: the overview's tiles, charts and tables fit on about one screen.

Every table pages (10/25/50/100 a page) and sorts by its columns; Runs now goes back through all history, filtered by player, mode, map, result, device and date; Players by name and ban status; Reports, live co-op sessions and versions have search boxes.

versions.title: The foundries get a second level
notes: Every one of the Forge's seven foundries has a raised steel deck up a flight of stairs at the back of the hall, railed along its open edges: somewhere to stand over the hall and shoot down while the forge catches.
The infected follow you up the stairs (they climb a step at a time and can no longer reach you from the floor below), and the squad follows you up too.
Shots, blasts and bodies thrown by them all work up there, in co-op as well.

versions.title: No first-time stutter, and themed scrollbars
notes: The reborn, the PROMETHEUS cutscene and the RPG no longer stutter the first time they appear: nothing adds a light mid-run any more (that recompiled every material), and their shaders and shapes are prepared while the map loads.
Scrollbars across the game and the bestiary are a thin amber rail in the game's style; the settings panel no longer shows a sideways scrollbar.

versions.title: The seven foundries
notes: The embers come from the seven named foundries (IGNIS, AMETHYST FLAME, KIZUNA SPARK, SAKURA SPARK, MOSSFIRE, VOID EMBER, FROSTFIRE), now brick halls spread around the Forge instead of one row.
Go in, stoke the forge and hold the hall for 30 seconds while a horde comes for it, wave after wave, until it catches.
The small round furnaces are gone.
Killed infected no longer float in the air lying flat: a body knocked over rests on the ground, and any still tumbling after 3 seconds settles.

versions.title: Standard Mazoku made plain, and version numbers
notes: Standard Mazoku is each map's own Standard operation plus the five card carriers and their side contract - nothing else (a test now checks it on every map).
Card texts no longer assume the District; the start banner matches Standard's.
The version shows faintly in the bottom-right corner of every screen, so screenshots and videos say which build they came from.
This changelog on the admin page.

versions.title: The Forge: the last of it
notes: The run starts in the Hearth: an open safe zone with a sentry gun that cuts down infected coming through the gate.
Seven of sixteen cold furnaces are drawn each run, one per ember (currency): stoke one, hold its circle for 30 seconds.
The last stand: once the bird is called, the infected come for the Hearth in waves.
The carrier convulses and glows before the turn; the infected pulse as the fire is drawn out of them.
The reborn has its own look: phoenix wings of flame and a crown of fire.
PROMETHEUS is a Vulcan orb that explains everything over the Forge, says it will be back, and leaves the sky.
Lore rewritten around the embers; new title menu objectives.

versions.title: Anime looks for riry and Athy
notes: riry and Athy drawn anime-style; Anya's long braids so she reads as a woman at a distance.

versions.title: The Forge, rekindled
notes: The Forge grew to 190 x 150 m with the Vulcan story: holdouts barricaded in safe rooms, two of Vulcan in the squad, tomoe in the vault.
Ledger pages, riry's Rumble Pit, a hidden-bite finale, the burnout at dawn and the closing cutscene.
Flow fields spread over frames for the bigger map.
